I have a core bit of body-weight exercises that I do (push-ups, sit-ups, obliques, biceps, triceps, calves, & squats). Depending on the game being played, you will have to adjust to make sure it works. In the end it is more or less the same, find natural breaks in game play and get up and exercise. Quest over, do a full set running through all exercises. All you did was beat an objective, do one exercise for 30 seconds. Waiting to respawn (depending on respawn time), pick one exercise and do it until your back in the game. Screen loading, pick an exercise and get to it. Game saved, pick three exercises and do them each for a minute.

I personally use this technique with everything. Load of laundry, exercise. Vacuum, exercise. Play music, exercise. Game, exercise. Bored staring all the walls trying to figure out what to do next, exercise. My 88 year old grandmother meeting her favorite Yankee, Tino Martinez - 2012 [OC]

This was taken at Old Timer's Day in 2012. My grandma lived in Fairfield County, CT, but hadn't been to a Yankee game since the mid 80s. She still watched every single game on TV though. She fully admitted however that she had trouble being as passionate about the Yanks since 2001, entirely because they traded away Tino.

The story of getting him into our box is one that makes me so appreciative of the family I have. My cousin Bryan heard that Tino was paying a visit to some people a few boxes over, so he heads down the hall to ask him to stop by and see my grandma. He doesn't get to talk to Tino, but he tells his handler the story and the handler says they'll try, but can't promise. Bryan comes back, but keeps an eye out for Tino. A few minutes later Tino with his security and handler walk past without stopping. Bryan runs after them trying to get Tino's attention. The security guys immediately turn around and make a wall (Bryan is 25 and built similarly to Tino). He tries to explain that my grandma is 88 and has been a Yankee fan since Gehrig played, but Tino is her favorite Yankee and she would love to meet him. Tino looks at his handler, the handler points at his watch, Tino looks back at my cousin (still being restrained) and says, "we will come back in a few minutes for a short visit."

I imagine it's how people feel who know they're going to meet the President. Bryan comes back and tells us all that Tino is going to come by. The buzz of 40 people all finding out at the same time that this 88 year old woman is going to meet her favorite ball player was incredible - all of us excited for her more than for ourselves.

Anyway - I thought the story added something worthwhile. My grandma passed away last November at 90 years old, and it makes me so happy to look back on her getting to meet Tino. If he didn't make time for that she would have never gotten another chance.
